headline: $18,225,000 bond for city facilities, roads, and sidewalks approved; $2.2 million vehicle bond tabled.
summary: The bond would pay for work such as fuel station tanks, roof repairs, and wastewater plant upgrades. Members also accepted a $1 million dam and seawall grant for electrical upgrades at flood control pump station number two. The $2.2 million vehicle bond is set to return at the December 8th finance meeting.
decisions: Approved accepting the $1 million Dam and Seawall Program grant.
Withdrew the motion to approve the vehicle bond with $350,000 removed.
Approved a $2 million vehicle bond, 5-0, and asked for a revised order.
Withdrew the $2 million vehicle bond motion so a new order can be filed.
Tabled the $2.2 million vehicle bond until the December 8th finance meeting, 4-1.
Approved the $18,225,000 bond for city facilities, roads, and sidewalks, 5-0.
Received the Department of Administration and Finance reorganization update, 5-0.
Referred the organizational chart to City Council, then to Ordinance, 5-0.
discussion: Vehicle bond amount: Members asked whether the vehicle line items matched the requests, and the $350,000 ambulance was dropped. Amounts of $1.85 million and $2 million were discussed before the item was tabled.

Debt capacity: Members asked whether the city can afford about $20 million in new bonds. The chief administration finance officer said debt payments are falling each year, so the city has room for the $20 million.

Projects in the $18,225,000 bond: Members asked whether items such as library or Wistariahurst repairs could be cut. Legal advice was that the council cannot reduce a bond order, so a new order would be needed.
Fuel station tanks: Two of eight dispensers are out of service, and the underground tank warranty expires in 2028. The project would replace the underground tanks with above-ground tanks.
